question: Should reply-session conflict classification become a permanent public `plugin-sdk/error-runtime` contract with the PR's strict exact-message semantics?
rationale: Bundled plugins need a shared owner boundary, but exporting this predicate commits OpenClaw to an externally consumable API and intentionally changes legacy classification semantics across several channels.

options.title: Approve the narrow SDK predicate
options.body: Accept the shared public classifier after documenting its compatibility semantics and proving the migrated retry behavior in a real runtime setup.

options.title: Keep classification internal
options.body: Avoid expanding the public SDK and instead provide a bundled-only runtime seam or retain local classifiers until a broader error-code contract exists.

options.title: Pause for typed error design
options.body: Defer this PR and define a stable machine-readable conflict code before migrating all channel retry paths.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow SDK predicate
recommendation.body: Accept the shared public classifier after documenting its compatibility semantics and proving the migrated retry behavior in a real runtime setup.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin SDK facade and surface-budget work makes this person the strongest history-backed owner for the public-contract decision.
